questions.chapter: Chapter 1: Introduction to Object-Oriented Programming and Principles
questions.text: Explain key Object-Oriented Programming principles: Encapsulation, Data Hiding, Abstraction, Inheritance, and Polymorphism. Compare Procedure-Oriented Programming (C) vs Object-Oriented Programming (C++).

questions.chapter: Chapter 2: Classes, Objects, Constructors and Destructors
questions.text: Explain different types of Constructors in C++: Default constructor, Parameterized constructor, Copy constructor (`ClassName(const ClassName &obj)`), and Dynamic constructor. Why does the copy constructor pass its argument by reference? Explain the role of Destructors.

questions.chapter: Chapter 6: Templates and Generic Programming (Function and Class Templates)
questions.text: What is a `friend` function and `friend` class? Why does a friend function violate data encapsulation? Write a C++ program with two classes `ClassA` and `ClassB` to find the maximum of two private data members using a common friend function.

questions.chapter: Chapter 3: Operator Overloading and User-Defined Type Conversions
questions.text: What is Operator Overloading? What are the rules and limitations of operator overloading in C++ (Which operators cannot be overloaded)? Overload the binary `+` operator and `==` comparison operator for a `Complex` number class $(a + ib)$ using: (a) Member functions, and (b) Friend functions.

questions.chapter: Chapter 6: Templates and Generic Programming (Function and Class Templates)
questions.text: Overload the stream insertion `<<` and stream extraction `>>` operators for a custom `Matrix` / `Time` class $(hours, minutes, seconds)$ using friend functions.

questions.chapter: Chapter 3: Operator Overloading and User-Defined Type Conversions
questions.text: Explain Type Conversions in C++: (a) Basic type to User-defined Class type (using Constructor), (b) User-defined Class type to Basic type (using Casting Operator function `operator type()`), and (c) One Class type to Another Class type (Conversion Routine in source class vs Destination constructor). Write code to convert `Polar(radius, angle)` to `Cartesian(x, y)`.

questions.chapter: Chapter 4: Inheritance (Single, Multiple, Hierarchical, Multilevel)
questions.text: Explain types of Inheritance: Single, Multiple, Multilevel, Hierarchical, and Hybrid inheritance. Explain the Diamond Problem in Hybrid Inheritance (Ambiguity). How does `virtual` base class resolve the diamond problem in C++?

questions.chapter: Chapter 5: Virtual Functions, Abstract Classes and Runtime Polymorphism
questions.text: What is Runtime Polymorphism (Dynamic Binding / Late Binding)? Explain Virtual Functions and Pure Virtual Functions (`virtual void func() = 0;`). What is an Abstract Base Class? Explain how the Virtual Method Table (`vtable`) and Virtual Pointer (`vptr`) implement dynamic dispatch at runtime.

questions.chapter: Chapter 5: Virtual Functions, Abstract Classes and Runtime Polymorphism
questions.text: Why do base classes with virtual functions require a `virtual destructor`? Explain what happens when a derived class object pointed to by a base class pointer is deleted without a virtual destructor (Memory leak).

questions.chapter: Chapter 6: Templates and Generic Programming (Function and Class Templates)
questions.text: Explain Function Templates and Class Templates with non-type parameters. Write a generic C++ Class Template for a `Stack<T>` data structure supporting `push()`, `pop()`, `top()`, and `isEmpty()` operations for any data type.

questions.chapter: Chapter 7: Exception Handling (try, catch, throw)
questions.text: Explain Exception Handling in C++: `try`, `catch`, and `throw` blocks. Explain Multiple `catch` blocks and Catch-All handler (`catch(...)`). Write a program to handle Divide-by-Zero and Array-Index-Out-of-Bounds exceptions using custom exception classes.

questions.chapter: Chapter 6: Templates and Generic Programming (Function and Class Templates)
questions.text: Explain C++ Stream Class Hierarchy (`ios`, `istream`, `ostream`, `iostream`, `ifstream`, `ofstream`, `fstream`). Explain file opening modes (`ios::in`, `ios::out`, `ios::app`, `ios::binary`, `ios::trunc`) and file pointers manipulation using `seekg()`, `seekp()`, `tellg()`, and `tellp()`.

questions.chapter: Chapter 1: Introduction to Object-Oriented Programming and Principles
questions.text: Write a C++ program to write an array of `Student` objects (RollNo, Name, GPA) to a binary file `students.dat` using `write()` and read them back into memory using `read()` to search for a student by roll number.

questions.chapter: Chapter 1: Introduction to Object-Oriented Programming and Principles
questions.text: Explain the three main components of the Standard Template Library (STL): Containers (Sequence: `vector, list, deque`; Associative: `map, set`), Iterators, and Algorithms (`sort(), find(), count()`). Write a program demonstrating `std::vector` and `std::map`.

questions.chapter: Chapter 2: Classes, Objects, Constructors and Destructors
questions.text: Explain `static` data members and `static` member functions in C++. Write a program to count the number of objects currently alive in memory using static variables and constructors/destructors.

questions.chapter: Chapter 3: Operator Overloading and User-Defined Type Conversions
questions.text: Overload unary prefix `++` and postfix `++` increment operators for a `Counter` class. Explain how the dummy `int` parameter distinguishes postfix from prefix in C++.

questions.chapter: Chapter 4: Inheritance (Single, Multiple, Hierarchical, Multilevel)
questions.text: Explain the order of execution of Constructors and Destructors in Multiple and Multilevel inheritance when parameterized constructors are present.

questions.chapter: Chapter 6: Templates and Generic Programming (Function and Class Templates)
questions.text: Write a generic function template to sort an array of any numeric type using the Bubble Sort algorithm. Explain Template Specialization for `char*` or specific data types.
